source_refs.note: Topic 23.7.1 (PDF 113); the equations are redrawn. The book numbers the methods i, iii and iv (no ii); the phenyl benzoate example follows the learning outcome.

items: From carboxylic acids and alcohols (Fischer esterification), in acid: CH3CH2COOH + CH3CH2OH <=> CH3CH2COOCH2CH3 + H2O (H+), giving ethyl propanoate. In general RCOOH + HOR' <=> RCOOR' + H2O: the C-OH bond of the acid and the O-H bond of the alcohol break.

From acyl chlorides and alcohols: acyl chlorides react vigorously with alcohols; the reaction goes to completion and does not form an equilibrium mixture: CH3COCl + CH3CH2OH -> CH3COOCH2CH3 + HCl (ethyl ethanoate).
From acyl chlorides and phenol: phenyl esters form when an acyl chloride is warmed with phenol; the reaction is discussed in Chapter 22.

blocks.alt: Propanoic acid, CH3-CH2-C(=O)-OH, + ethanol, CH3-CH2-OH, with H+ over equilibrium arrows, gives ethyl propanoate, CH3-CH2-C(=O)-O-CH2-CH3, + H2O.

blocks.alt: R-C(=O)-OH + H-O-R, with H+ over equilibrium arrows, gives R-C(=O)-OR + H2O. Two arrows labelled 'Bond Cleavage' point at the C-OH bond of the acid and the H-O bond of the alcohol.
